week_1_baby_dev: The pregnancy process begins with the first day of your last menstrual period. Your body is preparing for conception and a new life.
week_1_mother_changes: Hormone levels begin to change, continue taking folic acid supplements (400-800 mcg) regularly.
week_2_baby_dev: Ovulation and conception occur. The foundations of genetic heritage are laid in this miraculous moment.
week_2_mother_changes: A slight increase in basal body temperature and hormonal changes begin.
week_3_baby_dev: The fertilized zygote rapidly divides to become a blastocyst and travels through the fallopian tubes to the uterus.
week_3_mother_changes: The uterine lining thickens; some mothers may feel slight implantation spotting or sensation.
week_4_baby_dev: The blastocyst has safely implanted in the uterus. The placenta and amniotic sac begin to form rapidly.
week_4_mother_changes: Missed period, slight sensitivity to smells, and fullness in the breasts may be felt.
week_5_baby_dev: The neural tube (brain and spinal cord outline) has begun to form. The heart tube is preparing for its first rhythmic movements.
week_5_mother_changes: Mild morning sickness, frequent urination, and fatigue may occur.
week_6_baby_dev: The tiny heart begins to beat at about 100-115 beats per minute. Arm and leg buds appear.
week_6_mother_changes: Sensitivity to smells may increase. Drinking plenty of fluids and resting is important.
week_7_baby_dev: The brain hemispheres are developing rapidly. Eye and ear vesicles begin to become pronounced.
week_7_mother_changes: Nausea may intensify. Ginger tea and dry crackers can be soothing.
week_8_baby_dev: The heart beats at about 150-160 times a minute. Finger and toe buds are elongating.
week_8_mother_changes: As the uterus continues to grow, slight groin pulls may be felt.
week_9_baby_dev: Eyelids and the tip of the nose are forming. Joints and muscles produce their first involuntary tiny movements.
week_9_mother_changes: Hormone-related mood swings are normal, take care to rest.
week_10_baby_dev: The embryonic period is complete, officially a fetus now! All vital organ outlines are completed.
week_10_mother_changes: The uterus has reached the size of an orange. A slight softening around the waist begins.
milestone_10_desc: To screen for chromosomal abnormalities (like Down Syndrome) with 99% accuracy using cell-free fetal DNA in the mother's blood, NIPT testing can be done starting from week 10.
milestone_10_action: Discuss the NIPT option with your doctor.
week_11_baby_dev: Bones are beginning to harden, nail beds and hair follicles are forming.
week_11_mother_changes: Nausea may gradually begin to ease, blood volume and circulation increase.
milestone_11_desc: Schedule your appointment for nuchal translucency (NT) ultrasound measurement and blood test (PAPP-A, free β-hCG).
milestone_11_action: Book a double test appointment between 11 and 13+6 weeks.
week_12_baby_dev: Reflexes are developing, fingers can open and close, and hiccup movements can be made.
week_12_mother_changes: The uterus rises out of the pelvis. Early pressure on the bladder somewhat decreases.
milestone_12_title: Double Marker Test and NT Measurement
milestone_12_desc: The most critical first-trimester screening, with nuchal translucency (NT) ultrasound and blood biochemistry, should be performed this week.
milestone_12_action: Discuss your double test results with your obstetrician.
week_13_baby_dev: Last week of the 1st Trimester! Vocal cords have formed, tiny fingerprints are taking shape.
week_13_mother_changes: Your energy gradually returns; improvements in your appetite begin.
week_14_baby_dev: Start of the 2nd Trimester! Facial muscles have developed, can frown or smile.
week_14_mother_changes: Your energy is returning, nausea largely subsides. The pregnancy glow period begins.
week_15_baby_dev: Can distinguish light. Thin legs are elongating and bone mineralization is accelerating.
week_15_mother_changes: Nasal congestion may be felt (pregnancy rhinitis); continue to drink plenty of water.
week_16_baby_dev: Eyes are sensitive to light. Legs are longer than arms and joints are extremely flexible.
week_16_mother_changes: Some mothers may begin to feel the first flutterings, like tiny butterfly wings.
milestone_16_desc: A biochemical screening test examining AFP, hCG, estriol, and inhibin-A values is planned during these weeks.
milestone_16_action: Consult your doctor if a double test was not done or if further evaluation is needed.
week_17_baby_dev: Skeleton is turning from cartilage into hard bone tissue. Begins to store fat tissue.
week_17_mother_changes: Your appetite may increase. Opt for healthy snacks and calcium-rich foods.
week_18_baby_dev: Ears are fully in place and can hear sounds! Listening to your voice and heartbeat.
week_18_mother_changes: Your blood pressure may drop slightly; be careful when standing up suddenly.
week_19_baby_dev: Specialized centers for smell, taste, hearing, vision, and touch are forming in the brain.
week_19_mother_changes: Slight stretching and a tendency for stretch marks on the skin may occur; apply moisturizing care.
week_20_baby_dev: Halfway there! Skin is covered with a protective creamy layer called vernix caseosa.
week_20_mother_changes: Your belly button may slightly pop out. Baby kicks are now distinctly felt.
milestone_20_desc: All of the baby's organs, brain, heart, spine, kidneys, and limbs are examined in millimeter detail by a perinatologist/specialist.
milestone_20_action: Make sure to have your Detailed Ultrasound appointment between 20-22 weeks.
week_21_baby_dev: Bone marrow has begun producing blood cells. Your baby is regularly swallowing amniotic fluid.
week_21_mother_changes: To prevent varicose veins and leg cramps, keep your feet elevated when resting.
week_22_baby_dev: Eyelids and eyebrows are fully formed. The sense of touch is extremely sensitive.
week_22_mother_changes: Your skin may look brighter. Regular walks are good for back pain.
week_23_baby_dev: Passed the half-kilo mark! The dreaming phase begins with rapid eye movements (REM sleep).
week_23_mother_changes: Slight edema may be felt in the ankles and wrists; balance your salt consumption.
week_24_baby_dev: Surfactant substance has begun to be produced in the lungs. Taste buds are fully developed.
week_24_mother_changes: Dry eyes and skin tightness may be felt, drink plenty of water.
milestone_24_desc: Pregnancy diabetes screening with a 50g glucose tolerance test is performed between weeks 24-28.
milestone_24_action: Have your fasting blood sugar and 50g glucose screening done.
week_25_baby_dev: Nostrils are opening and practicing breathing movements.
week_25_mother_changes: Heartburn and indigestion complaints may increase; try eating small, frequent meals.
week_26_baby_dev: Begins to open their eyes. Lung vascularization is progressing rapidly.
week_26_mother_changes: Braxton Hicks practice contractions may start to be felt slightly.
week_27_baby_dev: Last week of the 2nd Trimester! Brain tissue is folding, expanding its surface area.
week_27_mother_changes: Lying on your left side while sleeping is ideal for blood circulation.
week_28_baby_dev: 3rd Trimester begins! Can open and close their eyes, enters REM sleep phase.
week_28_mother_changes: Slight swelling in ankles and shortness of breath may be felt, take care to rest.
milestone_28_title: Anti-D Injection & Start of NST Checks
milestone_28_desc: If the mother is Rh (-) negative and the father is Rh (+) positive, the blood incompatibility injection (Anti-D immunoglobulin) is administered this week. Routine NST monitoring is planned.
milestone_28_action: If your blood type is Rh negative, remind your doctor about the Anti-D injection.
week_29_baby_dev: Muscles and lungs are getting stronger. Reacts to the surroundings by moving their head.
week_29_mother_changes: The urge to urinate frequently may increase again due to uterine pressure on the bladder.
week_30_baby_dev: Bone marrow has fully taken over red blood cell production. Begins to regulate body temperature.
week_30_mother_changes: In case of heartburn and reflux, take care to eat small and frequent meals.
week_31_baby_dev: All 5 basic senses are active! Can easily turn their head from side to side.
week_31_mother_changes: A great week to start making your hospital bag checklist.
week_32_baby_dev: All nails have grown out, bones are strong. Continues to store fat and get chubby.
week_32_mother_changes: Braxton Hicks contractions may become noticeable; do relaxing breathing exercises.
week_33_baby_dev: The immune system is strengthening with antibodies passed from the mother. Bones have fully hardened.
week_33_mother_changes: Pressure may be felt in the pelvic area; opt for comfortable shoes.
week_34_baby_dev: Lung development is largely complete. The skin has turned pink and is becoming smooth.
week_34_mother_changes: Increase your resting intervals, avoid lifting heavy loads.
week_35_baby_dev: Kidneys are fully functional. Most babies take the head-down birth position around these weeks.
week_35_mother_changes: As the baby drops lower, your heartburn may ease but bladder pressure increases.
week_36_baby_dev: Has started to take the birth position. Sucking and swallowing coordination is flawless.
week_36_mother_changes: Weekly doctor check-ups and NST monitoring may begin.
week_37_baby_dev: Early Term! Your baby is now medically ready to be born.
week_37_mother_changes: Be alert for signs of labor such as bloody show or water leaking.
week_38_baby_dev: Organs are fully matured. The lanugo hair on the skin has almost completely shed.
week_38_mother_changes: Be prepared to track labor pains and contraction intervals.
week_39_baby_dev: Full Term! Your baby continues to receive antibodies through the cord and store strength.
week_39_mother_changes: Go to the hospital immediately when contractions are 5 minutes apart or your water breaks.
week_40_baby_dev: The big day has arrived! Your baby is completely ready and waiting to meet you.
week_40_mother_changes: Notify your doctor immediately in case of regular contractions, bloody show, or water leaking.

emergency_sign_7_desc: Clear fluid leaking from vagina or sudden gush of water.

legal_item_1_title: 1. Not a Medical or Diagnostic Device
legal_item_1_desc: Aura Pregnancy is a digital tracking and wellness guide designed solely for lifestyle and personal logging. It does not provide medical diagnoses, prescribe treatments, or serve as a clinical decision support system.
legal_item_2_desc: Weekly fetal growth milestones, weight/length estimates, calorie/nutrition tips, and physical activity guidelines are general references compiled from international standards (ACOG, WHO, IOM). Every pregnancy is unique; always consult your obstetrician/gynecologist for personalized healthcare decisions.
legal_item_3_desc: In case of severe abdominal or head pain, sudden vaginal bleeding, fluid leakage, sudden decrease in fetal movement, vision disturbances, or fever above 38°C (100.4°F), immediately call emergency services (112 / 911) or visit the nearest emergency department.
legal_item_4_desc: All vital health logs (blood pressure, temperature, weight, kicks, medications, memories, and photos) are stored securely on your local device. Your personal data is never transmitted to external servers or third parties.
disclaimer_bp_fever: Blood pressure and temperature records are for personal logging. Consult your physician for abnormal or concerning readings.
disclaimer_kick_counter: Kick counter is intended for fetal movement awareness. Contact your doctor immediately if you notice a significant decrease in movements.
onboarding_disclaimer_notice: By using the app, you acknowledge and agree to the Medical Disclaimer & Legal Terms.

• Express a drop of breast milk onto your nipple after feeding for natural soothing.
